transcript:
Section A

News Report One
Officials said six residents had to move to another place after a building fire broke out on Main Street Saturday. Deputy Fire Chief Markowitz responded to a reported structure fire shortly after 1 p.m. Markowitz said crews encountered heavy smoke coming from the second floor when they arrived. A team of about 25 firefighters spent about 25 minutes extinguishing the flames. The building is described as a mixed-use building that features commercial businesses on the first floor and residential apartments on the second and third floors. Town records list four apartments in the building. [1] Due to smoke and heat damage, the four apartments were uninhabitable, and six residents had to relocate. There were no injuries reported. [2] The Norwalk Fire Marshal is investigating the cause and origin of the fire.

News Report Two
A new study has cast doubt on historic research suggesting that the season or month of one's birth is associated with an increased risk of certain mental health conditions. The new study looks at symptoms of anxiety and depression among more than 70,000 older adults in Europe. [3] A number of past studies have found the link between season of birth and mental health diagnoses. Researchers have suggested that such links could arise from various things. These factors include nutrient intake, sun exposure, climate, and disease exposure in a year's time. However, the evidence has been mixed. More recent studies have suggested that such factors as social class or economic background have more to do with these mental health diagnoses than month of birth. [4] Overall, the new study found no significant relationship between participants' month of birth and symptoms of depression or anxiety. The study involved some 70,000 adults in Europe. It found that as people age, the risk factors for depression shift somewhat depending on birth month. People may place more value on social class or background factors than on their month of birth. Some countries reported slightly different seasonal patterns. Overall, no systematic pattern was found.

News Report Three
Genetic researchers in China have made a clone of a star police dog. The clone was born in December in a laboratory in Beijing. The cloned dog and its mother are almost identical genetically. The mother dog helped solve multiple murder cases and other serious crimes. [5] In multiple tests, the clone has already performed better than traditionally bred dogs. [6] If the clone continues to perform as well as expected, it could mean a huge reduction in the training time for police dogs, which usually takes five years. The ultimate goal of the scientists is to create police dogs that can be trained in months instead of years. [7] However, due to the current cost, this goal is not yet possible. It is not the first time a clone has been made of a star police dog. In South Korea, six cloned dogs began working with the police in 2008.

Section B

Conversation One
M: Tom, did you see the article online about the new TV series based on the book The Three Body Problem?
W: [8] A colleague mentioned the book, but I've been so busy writing my thesis that I haven't been able to read for pleasure in months.
M: Well, sounds like if you're going to read anything for fun, this is the book. It's written by a Chinese science fiction writer. [9] I can't remember his name, but he's written three books, and all three are in the series. The Three Body Problem is the first one. I don't want to say too much, but it's definitely got some amazing technological and sociological concepts in it.
M: It should sound really interesting and fits my taste, but if they are making a TV series based on it, I don't know if I should read the book or watch the show first.
W: I think it's better to read the book first. Very few TV shows or movies are better than the book. If the show turns out not good, you'll have ruined this book.
M: When is the show supposed to start? [10] I've still got a bit overwhelmed with the amount of data I need to collect to finish my thesis. I still need to relax sometimes.
W: I can't remember exactly. It's pretty soon, and it's going to be quite long. There are 24 episodes. [11] Well, maybe you could download an electronic copy of the book and try to read it before the show starts.
M: That's a good idea. Then, and maybe we can watch this TV series together. Thanks for the tip, Alice.
W: No problem.

Conversation Two
W: Hello, good afternoon. [12] I have an inquiry to make. It's about the vegetarian food festival you are holding on the 19th of August at the Newcastle City Hall.
M: Yes, of course. My name is Philip. How can I help you?
W: [13] It says on your website that you are still looking for vendors, and I grow organic vegetables on my farm, as well as doing my own home baking. I would be able to sell both vegetables and homemade baked goods at the festival.
M: That's exactly the type of thing we are looking for. [14] However, we are getting close to the deadline. Do you prefer to fill out an application on the web, or to print it out and fill it in by hand? Remember that you will need to have all your certificates, because our standards are quite high. After the festival starts, we will carefully check everyone's certificates, as they are still running a small farm shop. We can submit our application on the website before the deadline, and we also have all the necessary certificates for running a small farm shop. Can you give me your details though?
M: Sure. Please address it to the Organization, Vendor Applications, 112 Queens Road, Newcastle, Northumbria. The postcode is NU 29 3LJ. [15] Remember that the closing date is next Tuesday, 28 of June.
W: That's absolutely wonderful. Thank you so much for your help. Goodbye.

Section C

Passage One
Supporters call it "wild camping"; opponents call it "illegal camping". Both sides admit that there has been a boom in the past few months, with increasing numbers of visitors pitching their tents on any bit of land they fancy in the UK. [16] In part, this reflects a fact that official campsites have been wholly or partially closed, or are operating at capacity in a summer when fewer people are going abroad. But this may also be an expression of a desire for going outdoors—a response to about months of isolation. Most of the coverage of the boom in wild camping has been negative. [17] In August and early September Britain has been banning in public parks. Even in Scotland, where camping is usually permitted on most of its open land, restrictions have been taking effect. Clearly, there have to be rules. [18] Wild campers need to ask for permission to camp from landowners, especially outside Scotland, where the law is far more restrictive. It would be common sense for people to use small tents and leave no trace of their visit. They have been attracted by a patch of land close to wilderness, and it is their responsibility to keep this patch of land the original way.

Passage Two
Imagine boating down the Amazon River, minding your own business—calmly keeping an eye out for alarmingly large snakes—and a curious pink dolphin appears to swim alongside. [19] While this may seem like a mythical creature, pink dolphins do exist in the Amazon region. The Amazon river dolphin is a giant among its species. It can measure up to 2 meters long and weigh about 204 kilograms. Size isn't the only thing that sets the Amazon river dolphin apart. Thriving in South American rivers and seasonal flood plains, this freshwater dolphin can even appear strikingly pink. Although born gray, males turn pink in adulthood, entering adulthood they will show distinct bright pink. [20] The unusual color is believed to be in fighting—either duels or competing for mates. The deeper the pink, the older the male, as the scar tissue accumulates. There is also a theory that this color helps dolphins blend into the environment more easily. During heavy rains, the Amazon rainforest rivers become pink, and it becomes easier to spot the pink dolphins. [21] Since 2018, this wetland system has been placed under international protection.

Passage Three
[22] In a new Merrill Lynch/Age Wave survey, a full 70% of early adults said they received financial support from their parents in the past year and 58% said they couldn't afford their current lifestyles without it. The most common types of financial support include cell phone plans, school costs, and car expenses. The executive of Age Wave, said parental financial support is now "the new normal". [23] But 64% of the young adults surveyed said parents' financial support to children 25 to 34 is "a bad thing", because this makes these kids dependent. It also mentioned that 59% thought it was fine to help adult children aged 18 to 24. But the remaining 71% thought that this assistance helps the adult children "get ahead". Dychtwald said the survey reveals that financial independence defines adulthood. [24] In fact, the respondents said, financial independence defines adulthood. [25] One big reason young adults are struggling is college loans, with average debt of $37,000. Many of the parents have taken on college loans for the kids too, sometimes even so they can study abroad. In the survey, 60% of young adults defined financial success as being debt-free. Whether that's possible, soon remains to be seen.

But then something changed.Instead of continuing to decline,the duration of the working week remained stable.It has stayed at just below 40 hours for nearly five decades.So what happened?Why are people working just as much today as in 1970?
